quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are only found in construction zones.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers important information. They help drivers stay in the correct position, show where it is safe to pass, and warn drivers about what is coming.

questions.question: To prepare for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and the sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your eyes in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and the sides.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Do not stare only at the center of the road. Keep looking at the entire road and its sides.

questions.question: When you cannot see well, your first action should be:
questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when you cannot see well or when road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead will split into two separate one-way roads. You must stay to the right.

questions.question: When following traffic across a railroad track with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing tracks.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and broken yellow line mark the center, and the broken line is next to you, you may pass if:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on one side and a broken yellow line on your side means you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:
questions.explanation: Leave more space in front of your vehicle when stopped going uphill. If the car ahead rolls backward, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Same side as traffic is moving.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use both inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always turn your head to check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast, your tires cannot clear water from the road. They lose their grip and the vehicle slides on a film of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: When two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different directions, which must yield?
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) does NOT depend on which of the following?

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. It is not affected by your physical fitness or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, you must pull over to let traffic pass if your slow driving is causing a backup.

questions.question: When must you pull over for an emergency vehicle?

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only drinking over the legal limit can
Even a small amount of alcohol can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol will reduce your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians on the road. Be especially careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: When a green arrow turns into a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How can road rage and aggressive driving be reduced?
questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey posted speed limits, and allow plenty of travel time.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less far ahead. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at an empty intersection at the same time, who goes first?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle arrives to your right at the same time, yield the right-of-way to that vehicle. You may then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing without lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to any oncoming trains before crossing, especially if there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle might stall.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: Yield to all emergency vehicles using a siren and flashing red, blue, or white lights. Pull to the right side of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing downward over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist does not obey traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
They will always get a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both motorists and bicyclists can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is nearby.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and yield the right-of-way to vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: Is checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes a good driving habit?

options.text: No, it is a bad habit.
Yes, it is a good habit.
No, not if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good habit.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: At four-way stops, all vehicles must stop. The first vehicle to reach the intersection goes first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report crashes to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how many inches from the curb should you park?
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels within 12 inches of the curb when parallel parking. Park only where it will not block traffic and where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel straight and slow down by easing off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel tight and keep the car going straight. Remove your foot from the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have control. Then brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: What time of day it is.
The condition and type of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: What time of day it is.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, road conditions, your vehicle's weight, your brakes, your tires, and your speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers that traffic is coming from the opposite direction. Warning signs are yellow with black markings.

questions.question: You are in the intersection waiting to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to get other drivers to let you through.
Go around the rear of a blocking car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways and listen for trains before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and shine back in your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption slightly, but cannot prevent impairment from too much drinking.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: You are driving in the right lane and want to move to the left lane. You should:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no vehicles are in the lane you want to enter. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll into the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: Driving at night requires extra caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder to see at night. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise or any time you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead has many curves and turns.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for conditions. Always follow the speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. Adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and the actions of other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move.
